title: Bekhorot 53
description: A new chapter on the tithe of animals opens: where and when the tithe applies, why it is no longer separated after the Temple’s destruction, why consecrated animals are not tithed, and which animals may be tithed together.
topics: 📖 Chapter 9 opens: the mitzva of animal tithe, in and outside the Land, with and without the Temple
🌍 Rabbi Akiva’s “tithes”: tithe from abroad is consecrated but not sacrificed
🏚️ Why no one tithes animals today: Rav Huna’s orphan, and Rabba’s fear of a mishap
🐂 The firstborn by contrast: selling the ears to a gentile, or Rabbi Yehuda’s blemish before birth
🎲 “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad”: no one knows which animal will come out tenth
🕊️ Why peace offerings are not tithed, and why “shall be sacred” was still needed
🐑 Sheep with goats, yes; new with old, no: “flock” against “year by year”
🌾 Teruma from one kind for another: “give the best of this and the best of that”

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, בַּחוּלִּין אֲבָל לֹא בַּמּוּקְדָּשִׁין. וְנוֹהֵג בַּבָּקָר וּבַצֹּאן, וְאֵינָן מִתְעַשְּׂרִים מִזֶּה עַל זֶה. בַּכְּבָשִׂים וּבָעִזִּים וּמִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה.

a2.he: בֶּחָדָשׁ וּבַיָּשָׁן, וְאֵינָן מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה. שֶׁהָיָה בַּדִּין, וּמָה אִם הֶחָדָשׁ וְהַיָּשָׁן שֶׁאֵינָן כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה אֵינָם מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, כְּבָשִׂים וְעִזִּים שֶׁהֵן כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְצֹאן״, מַשְׁמַע כׇּל צֹאן אֶחָד.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְיַקְרִיבֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם וְאֵת מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם״.

a4.he: בִּשְׁתֵּי מַעַשְׂרוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, אֶחָד מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן, מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, וּמִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן אִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה!

a5.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כָּאן לִיקְרַב, כָּאן לִיקְדַּשׁ. דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָא נָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא ״וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה״, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a6.he: אִי הָכִי, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָרֵב, אַמַּאי קָדוֹשׁ? לְנֶאֱכָל בְּמוּמוֹ לַבְּעָלִים.

a7.he: בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת. אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ הָאִידָּנָא נָמֵי! כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם יָתוֹם.

a8.he: אִי הָכִי, מֵעִיקָּרָא נָמֵי לָא! אֶלָּא, אֶפְשָׁר בְּהַכְרָזָה. הָכָא נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר בְּהַכְרָזָה!

a9.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: מִשּׁוּם תַּקָּלָה, וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּחָיְישִׁינַן לְתַקָּלָה? דִּתְנַן: אֵין מַקְדִּישִׁין, וְאֵין מַעֲרִיכִין, וְאֵין מַחְרִימִין בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה.

a10.he: וְאִם הִקְדִּישׁ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ וְהֶחְרִים, בְּהֵמָה — תֵּיעָקֵר, פֵּירוֹת כְּסוּת וְכֵלִים — יֵרָקְבוּ, מָעוֹת וּכְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת — יוֹלִיךְ לְיָם הַמֶּלַח. וְאֵיזֶהוּ עִיקּוּר? נוֹעֵל דֶּלֶת בְּפָנֶיהָ וְהִיא מֵתָה מֵאֵילֶיהָ.

a11.he: אִי הָכִי, בְּכוֹר נָמֵי לָא לִיקְדֹּשׁ! בְּכוֹר בְּדִידַן תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא? בְּרֶחֶם קָדוֹשׁ! הָכִי קָאָמַר: לִיקְנִינְהוּ לְאוּדְנַיְיהוּ לְגוֹיִם, דְּלָא לִיקְדֹּשׁ מֵעִיקָּרָא!

b1.he: אֶפְשָׁר כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מוּתָּר לוֹ לָאָדָם לְהַטִּיל מוּם בִּבְכוֹר קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם. הָכָא נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר דְּשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא!

b2.he: מִי יָדַע הֵי נָפֵיק? וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ בְּרֵישׁ עַשְׂרָה — ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא.

b3.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֶפְשָׁר דְּשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ — מְהֵרָה יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וּבָעֵינַן בְּהֵמָה לְהַקְרָבָה וְלֵיכָּא.

b4.he: הָכִי נָמֵי בִּבְכוֹר בְּהֵמָה, מְהֵרָה יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וּבָעֵינַן בְּהֵמָה לְהַקְרָבָה וְלֵיכָּא! אֶפְשָׁר בִּפְשׁוּטִין.

b5.he: הָכָא נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר בִּלְקוּחִין! כֵּיוָן דְּאִיהוּ שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ, וּשְׁכִיחִי מוּמֵי דְּפָסְילִי בְּקָדָשִׁים, דַּאֲפִילּוּ דּוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן נָמֵי פָּסְלִי — לָא שְׁכִיחִי.

b6.he: בַּחוּלִּין אֲבָל לֹא בַּמּוּקְדָּשִׁין. מוּקְדָּשִׁין — פְּשִׁיטָא, לָאו דִּידֵיהּ נִינְהוּ!

b7.he: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאָמַר: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הֵם. דְּתַנְיָא: ״וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁהֵן מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא לִיעַשְּׂרוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b8.he: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי! ״יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא שֶׁכְּבָר קָדוֹשׁ.

b9.he: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״, הָא לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא חָיְילָא קְדוּשַּׁת מַעֲשֵׂר עִילָּוַיְהוּ? הַשְׁתָּא קְדוּשָּׁה חֲמוּרָה אַקְּדוּשָּׁה קַלָּה לָא חָיְילָא, קְדוּשָּׁה קַלָּה אַקְּדוּשָּׁה קַלָּה מִיבַּעְיָא?!

b10.he: מַאי הִיא? דִּתְנַן: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, אֵין מְשַׁנִּין אוֹתָם מִקְּדוּשָּׁה לִקְדוּשָּׁה, אֲבָל מַקְדִּישִׁין אוֹתָן הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִילּוּי, וּמַחְרִימִין אוֹתָן.

b11.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם, דְּכׇל בְּהֵמָה לָאו לְעוֹלָה קָיְימָא, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּכׇל בְּהֵמָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר קָיְימָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאַקְדְּשַׁהּ — לָא פָּקַע אִיסּוּרָא דְּמַעֲשֵׂר מִינַּהּ.

b12.he: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? בְּ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ וּבְ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b13.he: וְנוֹהֵג בַּבָּקָר וּבַצֹּאן, וְאֵין מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, בַּכְּבָשִׂים וּבָעִזִּים וְכוּ׳. וְיִהְיוּ חָדָשׁ וְיָשָׁן מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר: וּמָה כְּבָשִׂים וְעִזִּים שֶׁהֵם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה — מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, חָדָשׁ וְיָשָׁן שֶׁאֵינָן כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּתְעַשְּׂרוּ מִזֶּה עַל זֶה?

b14.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״ בִּשְׁתֵּי מַעַשְׂרוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, אֶחָד מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן, וּמַקִּישׁ מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן: מָה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן מֵחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן לֹא, אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מֵחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן לֹא.

b15.he: אִי הָכִי, כְּבָשִׂים וְעִזִּים נָמֵי לֵימָא: מַקִּישׁ מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה לְמַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן — מָה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ לֹא, אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ לֹא? רַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״צֹאן״.

b16.he: אִי הָכִי, חָדָשׁ וְיָשָׁן נָמֵי! הָא כְּתִיב ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״. וּמָה רָאִיתָ? אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״שָׁנָה שָׁנָה״ — לְשָׁנָה הִקַּשְׁתִּיו, וְלֹא לְדָבָר אַחֵר.

b17.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, וְאִם תָּרַם — אֵין תְּרוּמָתוֹ תְּרוּמָה. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב יִצְהָר וְכׇל חֵלֶב תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן״ — אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: תֵּן חֵלֶב לָזֶה וְחֵלֶב לָזֶה.

messages.text: Chapter 9 · מעשר בהמה · Ma’aser Behema: the tithe of animals. Chapter 8 ended on 52b.
Mishna
The mitzva of animal tithe is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael, in the presence of, i.e., in the time of, the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.

notes.he: בכל מקום רגיל להזכיר בכור ומעשר ופסח ששוין במתנותיהן להכי תנא מעשר אגב בכור ופסח דנפישי מיליה תנא בפסחים:
notes.en: Animal tithe etc.: everywhere it is usual to mention the firstborn, the tithe and the Paschal offering together, since their blood placements are alike. So the tithe is taught alongside the firstborn, and the Paschal offering, whose laws are many, is taught in Pesaḥim.

notes.he: הא דאמרי' בריש שילוח הקן (חולין דף קלח:) דכל היכא דתנא בארץ ובחוצה לארץ שלא לצורך לבד מראשית הגז היינו בהנהו דתנן בההיא מכילתא אבל הכא לצורך הוא:
notes.en: Is in effect in the Land and outside the Land: what we say at the beginning of Shiluaḥ HaKen (Ḥullin 138b), that wherever “in the Land and outside the Land” is taught it was unnecessary, except for the first of the shearing, refers to those taught in that tractate; but here it is necessary.

notes.he: לאחר חרבן הבית:
notes.en: Not in the presence of the Temple: after the destruction of the Temple.

messages.text: It is in effect with regard to non-sacred animals but not with regard to sacrificial animals.

And it is in effect with regard to the herd and the flock, but they are not tithed from one for the other; and it is in effect with regard to sheep and goats, and they are tithed from one for the other.

notes.dh: מתני' מעשר בהמה כו' בכבשים ובעזים
notes.he: כלומר ונוהג בכבשים ועזים:
notes.en: Mishna. Animal tithe etc. With sheep and with goats: that is, and it is in effect with sheep and goats.

messages.text: And it is in effect with regard to animals from the new flock and with regard to animals from the old flock, but they are not tithed from one for the other.

notes.he: שנולדו לאחר אלול:
notes.en: New: those born after [the first of] Elul.

notes.he: שנולדו קודם אלול:
notes.en: Old: those born before Elul.

notes.dh: ואין מתעשרין חדש וישן מזה על זה
notes.he: כדמפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: And new and old are not tithed from one for the other: as the Gemara explains.

notes.dh: בחדש ובישן ואינן מתעשרין מזה על זה
notes.he: באותן שנולדו לפני אלול ולאחר אלול אין מתעשרין מזה על זה החדש על הישן:
notes.en: [A printer’s note: the comments from “with new and old” up to “just as grain tithe” belong to the mishna.] With new and old, and they are not tithed from one for the other: those born before Elul and those born after Elul are not tithed from one for the other, the new for the old.

messages.text: As by right, it should be inferred: If in the case of animals from the new flock and the old flock, which do not carry the prohibition of mating diverse kinds when mated with each other because they are one species, are nevertheless not tithed from one for the other, then with regard to sheep and goats, which do carry the prohibition of mating diverse kinds when mated with each other, is it not right that they will not be tithed from one for the other?

notes.he: שהיה בדין שכבשים ועזים לא יתעשרו מזה על זה מה אם החדש על הישן שאינו כלאים זה בזה הנולד מהן אינו כלאים:
notes.en: For by right sheep and goats should not be tithed from one for the other: for if new for old, which are not diverse kinds with each other, and what is born of them is not diverse kinds, [may not be tithed from one for the other, then all the more so sheep and goats].

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord,” indicating that with regard to animal tithe, all animals that are included in the term flock are one species.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: ת"ל וצאן כל משמע כל צאן אחד כלומר כל דכתב כל מעשר בקר שדי ההוא כל אוצאן דליהוי משמע כל צאן אחד וכבשים ועזים איקרו צאן דכתיב ואם מן הצאן קרבנו מן הכבשים או מן העזים:
notes.en: The verse states “flock … all”: implying that all flock is one. That is, the “all” written in “all the tithe of the herd,” throw that “all” onto “flock,” so that it implies all flock is one; and sheep and goats are called flock, as it is written: “And if his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats” (Leviticus 1:10).

messages.text: Gemara
Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.
messages.quote: in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael

notes.he: דקתני נוהג בחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: Gemara. Let us say the mishna: which teaches that it is in effect outside the Land.

messages.text: One might have thought that a person must bring up his animal tithe from outside of Eretz Yisrael and sacrifice it in the Temple. Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall bring there your burnt offerings, and your offerings, and your tithes, and the offering of your hand, and your vows, and your gift offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.”

verse.he: וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם וְאֵת מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם וְאֵת תְּרוּמַת יֶדְכֶם וְנִדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקַרְכֶם וְצֹאנְכֶם׃
verse.en: and there you are to bring your burnt offerings and other sacrifices, your tithes and contributions, your votive and freewill offerings, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks.

notes.dh: רבי עקיבא אומר יכול יעלה אדם מעשר כו'
notes.he: בתמורה בסוף אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כא:) קאמר נמי רבי עקיבא הכי דבכור הבא מחוצה לארץ אינו קרב דמוקי התם מתני' דמס' חלה (פ"ד מי"א) דבן אנטיגנוס העלה בכורות מבבל ולא קבלום ממנו כר' עקיבא:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva says: Might a person bring up tithe, etc.: in Temura, at the end of Elu Kodashim (Temura 21b), Rabbi Akiva also says this, that a firstborn coming from outside the Land is not sacrificed. For there the Gemara establishes the mishna in tractate Ḥalla (4:11), that Ben Antigonus brought up firstborns from Babylonia and they did not accept them from him, as following Rabbi Akiva.

messages.text: The plural form “tithes” indicates that the verse is speaking of two tithes; one is the animal tithe, and the other one is the second tithe of grain, i.e., produce.

notes.he: אינו נוהג אלא בארץ דקאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף לז.) כל מצוה שהיא חובת קרקע אינה נוהגת אלא בארץ וילפינן ליה מקראי:
notes.en: Tithe of grain: is in effect only in the Land, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (37a): every mitzva that is an obligation of the land is in effect only in the Land; and we derive it from verses.

messages.text: Since these two tithes are included in the same word, it is derived from here that from the place where you bring up the tithe of grain, i.e., Eretz Yisrael, as the obligation to separate tithe of grain applies only there, you also bring up the animal tithe; but from a place where you do not bring up the tithe of grain, i.e., outside of Eretz Yisrael, you do not bring up the animal tithe either.

notes.dh: ממקום שאי אתה מעלה מעשר דגן
notes.he: מחוצה לארץ לארץ וכל היכא דכתיב מעשר ותרומה באוריית' משמע בדגן שבארץ דסמיך ליה ארצם או נחלה כגון כי את מעשר בני ישראל אשר ירימו נתתי ללוים על כן אמרתי להם בתוך בני ישראל לא ינחלו נחלה. וכגון כי תכלה לעשר וגו' השקיפה וגו' אי אתה מעלה מעשר בהמה ומתניתין דקתני נוהג בארץ ובחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: From a place where you do not bring up grain tithe: from outside the Land to the Land. Wherever tithe and teruma are written in the Torah, it means grain of the Land, since land or inheritance is mentioned beside it, for example: “For the tithe of the children of Israel which they set apart … I have given to the Levites; therefore I said to them, among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance” (Numbers 18:24), and for example: “When you have finished tithing … look down …” (Deuteronomy 26:12–15). [So from there] you do not bring up animal tithe. And yet the mishna teaches that it is in effect in the Land and outside the Land.

messages.text: This baraita, which states the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, apparently contradicts the ruling of the mishna.

You may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, as the baraita and the mishna are referring to different cases. The baraita there is referring to the requirement to bring the animal tithe to Jerusalem for it to be sacrificed on the altar. By contrast, the mishna here is speaking of the status of every tenth animal; these animals are to be separated and consecrated.
messages.quote: bring up his animal tithe from outside of Eretz Yisrael and sacrifice it

notes.he: לאו קדוש. ומתני' דקתני נוהג ליקדש קאמר ומפרש בסמוך למאי הלכתא קדוש:
notes.en: To be sacrificed: [Rabbi Akiva excludes it from being sacrificed,] not from becoming sacred. And the mishna, which teaches that it is in effect, means that it becomes sacred; and the Gemara explains shortly for what halakha it is sacred.

notes.dh: אפי' תימא ר' עקיבא כאן ליקרב כאן ליקדש
notes.he: האי דקאמר רבי עקיבא אי אתה מעלה מחוצה לארץ ליקרב קאמר אבל מיקדש קדיש אפי' בחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: You may even say Rabbi Akiva: here, to be sacrificed; there, to be consecrated. When Rabbi Akiva says you do not bring it up from outside the Land, he means to be sacrificed; but it is consecrated even outside the Land.

messages.text: The language of the baraita is also precise, as it adduces a derivation from the phrase “and you shall bring there.” Conclude from this citation that the baraita is referring specifically to the requirement to bring the animal tithe and sacrifice it in Jerusalem.

notes.he: דר"ע מהקרבה הוא דקממעט לה מדנסיב הש"ס למילתיה מוהבאתם שמה דהיינו הקרבה:
notes.en: The language is also precise: that Rabbi Akiva excludes it from sacrifice, since the teaching takes his statement from “and you shall bring there,” which is sacrifice.

notes.he: דקרא ליקרב קאמר דכתיב והבאתם ומהקרבה הוא דמעטיה אבל מקדושה לא:
notes.en: The language is also precise: that the verse speaks of sacrifice, since it is written “and you shall bring,” and it is from sacrifice that he excludes it, but not from sanctity.

messages.text: If so, since animal tithe outside of Eretz Yisrael is not sacrificed on the altar, why is it consecrated? What is the significance of its sanctity?
It is consecrated to the extent that it may be eaten by its owner only when it develops a blemish.

notes.he: דימתין עד שיומם ואוכלן. מעשר בהמה בין תם בין בעל מום דבעלים הוא דלא אשכחן קרא דליתביה לכהן:
notes.en: With its blemish: he waits until it becomes blemished and eats it. Animal tithe, whether unblemished or blemished, belongs to the owners, since we find no verse saying it is given to the priest.

notes.he: ולא כשהוא תם:
notes.en: To be eaten with its blemish: and not when it is unblemished.

messages.text: If so, then even nowadays the halakha of the animal tithe should be in effect. Why then do people not remove every tenth animal from their flock or herd?
messages.quote: in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple

notes.he: בזמן הזה יהא נוהג:
notes.en: If so, even nowadays: let it be in effect in our time.

messages.text: The reason is in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna, as he says:

This is a rabbinic decree due to an orphan, i.e., a baby animal whose mother died before it was born, lest it be included with the other animals to be tithed; the obligation of animal tithe does not apply to it.

notes.he: לקמן בהאי פירקא (בכורות דף נח:):
notes.en: In accordance with Rav Huna, who said: later in this chapter (Bekhorot 58b).

notes.he: ה"נ גזרה משום יתום שלא יכניס יתום לדיר להתעשר דאמר במתני' הכל נכנסים לדיר להתעשר חוץ מכלאים וטריפה ויוצא דופן ומחוסר זמן ויתום. ולהכי נקט רב הונא יתום טפי מכל הני משום דהתם גבי מילתיה לא שייך למימר אלא לקוח ויתום לקמן בהאי פירקא. יתום שמתה אמו בשעת לידה זה פירש למיתה וזה פירש לחיים:
notes.en: A decree due to an orphan: here too [nowadays] it is a decree due to an orphan, lest one bring an orphan into the pen to be tithed; for the mishna [58b] says: all enter the pen to be tithed except diverse kinds, a tereifa, one born by caesarean section, one lacking in time [too young] and an orphan. Rav Huna names the orphan rather than any of the others because there, in the context of his statement, only “a purchased animal and an orphan” are relevant, later in this chapter. An orphan: whose mother died at the time of birth, “this one departed to death and that one departed to life.”

notes.dh: כרב הונא דאמר רב הונא גזירה משום יתום
notes.he: דרב הונא לקמן בפירקין (בכורות דף נח:) כיצד מעשרן ושם לא שייך למיגזר משום כלאים וטריפה ויוצא דופן אבל כאן שייך למיגזר משום הנהו כמו משום יתום אלא איידי דנקט רב הונא התם נקטה הכא ומיהו תימה דלא נקט לקוח ויתום כדנקט התם לכך נראה לי לפרש דנקט הכא דוקא יתום דטעו ביה טפי מבאחריני משום דלא בקיאי דיתום נמי לא משכחת ליה אלא בזה פירש למיתה וזה פירש לחיים:
notes.en: In accordance with Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said: a decree due to an orphan: Rav Huna’s statement is later in our chapter (Bekhorot 58b), at “How does one tithe them,” and there a decree due to diverse kinds, a tereifa or one born by caesarean section is not relevant. Here, though, a decree due to those would be as relevant as one due to an orphan; but since Rav Huna mentioned the orphan there, it is mentioned here. Yet it is puzzling that he does not say “a purchased animal and an orphan,” as he says there. So it seems to me that he mentions the orphan here specifically because people err about it more than about the others, since they are not expert in it, for an orphan too exists only where “this one departed to death and that one departed to life.”

notes.he: שלא יכניסו לדיר להתעשר ולאו בר עשורי הוא כדתנן במתניתין:
notes.en: A decree due to an orphan: lest they bring it into the pen to be tithed, though it is not subject to tithing, as we learned in the mishna.

messages.text: If so, then even originally, when the Temple stood, the practice should have also been not to separate animal tithe in case an orphaned animal was included in the counting.

notes.he: כשהמקדש קיים נגזור משום יתום:
notes.en: Originally too: when the Temple stood, let us decree due to an orphan.

notes.he: בפני הבית נמי לא משום יתום:
notes.en: Originally too: in the presence of the Temple too, [let there be no tithe] due to an orphan.

messages.text: Rather, there was no concern for an orphaned animal when the Temple stood, as it was possible to remove this concern by issuing an announcement to everyone that an orphaned animal is exempt from animal tithe.

notes.he: להכי לא גזרינן בזמן בית המקדש דאפשר בהכרזת ב"ד שלא יכניס אדם יתום לדיר להתעשר הילכך האידנא נמי ליפרשו ואפשר בהכרזה:
notes.en: Rather: the reason we did not decree in the time of the Temple is that it was possible by an announcement of the court that no one bring an orphan into the pen to be tithed. So nowadays too, let them separate it, since an announcement is possible.

messages.text: Here too, it is possible to remove the concern by means of an announcement that an orphaned animal is exempt from animal tithe.

notes.he: דמכרזי דיתום לאו בר עשורי:
notes.en: It is possible by an announcement: that they announce that an orphan is not subject to tithing.

messages.text: The reason animal tithe is no longer separated is due to concern that a mishap might occur.

notes.he: דאין לנו על מה להקריב וצריך לשהויי עד שיומם ואתי ביה לידי תקלה דגיזה ועבודה או שוחטו בלא מום:
notes.en: Due to a mishap: since we have nowhere to sacrifice, he would have to keep it until it becomes blemished, and he would come to a mishap with it: shearing it and working it, or slaughtering it without a blemish.

notes.he: משמע הכא דאין מעשר בהמה נוהג בזמן הזה משום תקלה והקשה ר"ת בפרק במה בהמה יוצאה (שבת נד:) דרבי אלעזר בן עזריה הוה מעשר תריסר אלפי עגלי מעדריה בכל שתא ולאחר החורבן היה דרבן יוחנן בן זכאי שהוא נשיא היה לאחר חורבן ואחריו רבן גמליאל ובימי רבן גמליאל מנו את ר' אלעזר בן עזריה נשיא כדאי' בפרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כז:) ובן י"ח שנה היה ואין לפרש כלל דאיירי בעישור שנותנין למלך כמו ארנונא ודוחק נמי לפרש דאפוטרופוס היה לו כשהוא קטן שהיה מעשר ושמא לא בטלו מעשר בהמה כ"כ סמוך לחורבן:
notes.en: Rather, due to a mishap: this implies that animal tithe is not in effect nowadays due to a mishap. Rabbeinu Tam asked from chapter Bameh Behema (Shabbat 54b): Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya used to tithe twelve thousand calves from his herds every year, and that was after the destruction. For Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, who was Nasi, lived after the destruction, and after him Rabban Gamliel, and in Rabban Gamliel’s days they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya Nasi, as stated in chapter Tefillat HaShaḥar (Berakhot 27b), when he was eighteen years old. One cannot at all explain that it speaks of a tenth given to the king, like a tax [arnona]; and it is also strained to explain that he had a guardian who tithed for him when he was a minor. Perhaps they did not abolish animal tithe so soon after the destruction.

notes.he: דשמא לא יכול להמתין עד שיומם ויאכלנו תם. ובזמן בהמ"ק ליכא למיחש לתקלה דהא מצי מקריב (לאימוריו) [לגבוה] בשעה שירצה ומצי למיכליה:
notes.en: Due to a mishap: lest he be unable to wait until it becomes blemished, and eat it unblemished. In the time of the Temple there is no concern about a mishap, since he can sacrifice it on high whenever he wishes, and he can eat it.

messages.text: And from where do you say that we are concerned for a mishap after the destruction of the Temple?

One may neither consecrate items, nor valuate an item’s worth based on its appraisal, nor dedicate items for sacred use (see Leviticus, chapter 27) and dedicate its monetary worth to the Temple treasury, in the present time, when the Temple is no longer standing.

notes.he: דחרם הויא קדש כהקדש דכתיב כל חרם קדש קדשים וגו':
notes.en: Nor dedicate [maḥarimin]: for a dedication [ḥerem] is sacred like consecrated property, as it is written: “every devoted thing is most holy” (Leviticus 27:28).

notes.he: אפילו למ"ד (ערכין דף כט.) סתם חרמים לכהנים אפי' במפרש לכהנים איכא למיגזר משום תקלה דכל זמן שהם ביד בעלים הרי הן הקדש כדאיתא לעיל בריש כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לב.) ובפ"ק דע"ז (דף יג.) פרש"י דקסבר סתם חרמים לבדק הבית ואי נמי כדפרי' והא דאמר עולא בערכין בסוף פרק המקדיש שדהו (ערכין דף כט.) אי הואי התם הוה יהיבנא כולהו לכהן דקסבר סתם חרמים לכהנים גבי ההוא גברא דאחרימנהו לנכסיה יש לחלק דהיינו במקרקעי דבלאו הכי מקשה ר"ת רב יהודה דסבר התם סתם חרמים לבדק הבית היכי שרי התם ע"י פדייה דלישקול ארבע זוזי ושדי בנהרא ואומר רבינו תם דהתם במקרקעות דאי אסרת להו איסור עולם כ"ש דאתי לידי תקלה טפי ומיהו קשה דמשמע התם דאיירי במטלטלין דפריך עלה מהא דתניא דאין שדה חרמים נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג ומשני הא במקרקעי הא במטלטלי וי"ל דמקרקעי חוצה לארץ קרי מטלטלי כדמסיק התם דכמטלטלי דמו ואע"ג דקאמר והא מעשה דפומבדיתא במקרקעי נמי הוה משמע מדקאמר נמי דהוה במקרקעי ובמטלטלי מ"מ לא התיר אלא המקרקעי לבד וכל שכן דניחא השתא דמכח זה פשיטא ליה להש"ס דבקרקעי נמי הוה עובדא דאי לא הוה התם אלא מטלטלי לא הוה שרי להו:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot explain that even according to the view that unspecified dedications go to the priests (Arakhin 29a), and even where one specified them for the priests, there is reason to decree due to a mishap, since as long as they are in the owner’s hands they are consecrated (above, Bekhorot 32a); in Avoda Zara (13a) Rashi explained that this baraita holds unspecified dedications go to Temple maintenance. As for Ulla in Arakhin (29a), “had I been there I would have given it all to the priest,” about the man who dedicated his property, one may say that case was land. Rabbeinu Tam asks how Rav Yehuda, who holds there that unspecified dedications go to Temple maintenance, permitted the property by redemption, “taking four zuz and throwing them into the river,” and answers that it was land, and forbidding land forever would lead all the more to a mishap. But that passage implies it was about movables, since it raises the teaching that a dedicated field applies only when the Jubilee applies, and answers “this is land, that is movables.” Tosafot answer that land outside the Land is called movables, as concluded there; and though the Pumbedita incident included land and movables, only the land was permitted, which fits the Talmud’s assumption that it included land, for had it been only movables he would not have permitted it. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.dh: אין מקדישין ואין מחרימין ואין מעריכין בזמן הזה
notes.he: דכל הני הוו לבדק הבית ואי אפשר למיצנעינהו עד שיבנה הבית ואתי בהו לידי תקלה הלכך [אם הקדיש] בהמה תעקר כו':
notes.en: One may not consecrate, nor dedicate, nor valuate nowadays: since all of these are for Temple maintenance, and it is impossible to store them away until the Temple is built, and one would come to a mishap with them. Therefore if he consecrated an animal, it should be uprooted, etc.

messages.text: And if one did consecrate, or valuate, or dedicate items for sacred use, the presence of these items might lead to the mishap of the violation of the prohibition against using consecrated property. Therefore, if one dedicated an animal it should be destroyed.

notes.he: דלא ליתי בה לידי תקלה:
notes.en: It should be uprooted: so that one not come to a mishap with it.

messages.text: If he dedicated produce, garments, or vessels made from materials that decompose, he should store them until they decompose. And if he dedicated money or metal vessels, he should take them and cast them into the Dead Sea.

notes.dh: מעות וכלי מתכות יוליך הנאה לים המלח
notes.he: משמע דוקא לים המלח ולא סגי בשאר נהרות וכן משמע בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כח.) דבשאר נהרות בעיא שחיקה אבל לים המלח מטיל בעיניה וכן בעלמא הפריש מעות לנזירותו ומת אמרינן יוליך הנאה לים המלח ותימה דבההוא עובדא דערכין (דף כט.) קאמר שקיל ארבע זוזי ושדי בנהרא וכן ביומא בפרק הוציאו לו (יומא דף נה:) קאמר ונשקול ארבעה זוזי ונשדי בנהרא ואידך לישתרו ושמא התם איירי על ידי שחיקה ועכשיו כשאדם בא לחלל כרם רבעי או נטע רבעי צריך לשחוק הנהו זוזי ומחלל עלייהו ולשדי בנהרא:
notes.en: Money and metal vessels he should take to the Dead Sea: this implies specifically the Dead Sea, and other rivers do not suffice. So too it is implied in chapter Kol Sha’a (Pesaḥim 28a) that in other rivers it needs grinding first, but into the Dead Sea one throws it as it is. And so elsewhere: one who set aside money for his naziriteship and died, we say he should take it to the Dead Sea. It is puzzling that in the incident in Arakhin (29a) it says he should take four zuz and throw them into the river, and likewise in Yoma, chapter Hotzi’u Lo (Yoma 55b), it says let us take four zuz and throw them into the river and let the rest be permitted. Perhaps there it speaks of grinding them. And now, when a person comes to redeem a fourth-year vineyard or fourth-year planting, he must grind the coins on which he redeems it and throw them into the river.

messages.text: And in the case of an animal, what constitutes uprooting? He locks the door before it, and it dies on its own from hunger.

notes.he: ברעב:
notes.en: It dies on its own: of hunger.

notes.dh: ואי זהו עיקור נועל דלת כו'
notes.he: בבכור בזמן הזה לא הוה שרינן למיעבד הכי דלא מיבעיא ישראל שיש לו לקיים מצות נתינה ולהמתין לכהן שירצה לקבלו אפי' יותר משלשים יום בדקה וחמשים בגסה דהא דתנן (לעיל בכורות דף כו:) עד כמה חייב ליטפל היינו אפי' בא כהן לקבלו תוך הזמן הזה כדקתני אמר לו הכהן בתוך הזמן תנהו לי הרי זה לא יתן אלא אפי' קבלו הכהן לא שרי ליה כהן לכונסו לכיפה דלא מישתמיט בשום דוכתא למתני הכי גבי בכור ולעיל (בכורות דף לה.) תנן בזכר של רחלים זקן ושערו מדולדל משמע שהיו רגילין להמתין עד שיפול בו מום ויש לחלק בין בכור למקדיש בזמן הזה דבכור דשרי בנפילת מום בלא פדייה איכא הפסד קדשים אם היה כונסו לכיפה אבל מקדיש דאפי' נפל בו מום לא שרי בלא פדיון ואי פריק ליה מיבעי להשליך הדמים לאיבוד הילכך כשכנסו עכשיו לכיפה אין כאן הפסד קדשים:
notes.en: And what is uprooting? He locks the door, etc.: with a firstborn nowadays we would not permit doing this. Not only an Israelite, who must fulfill the mitzva of giving it and wait for a priest who wants to accept it, even more than thirty days for a small animal and fifty for a large one (for what we learned above, Bekhorot 26b, “how long is he obligated to tend to it,” applies even if a priest came to accept it within that time, as it teaches: if the priest said to him within that time, “Give it to me,” he should not give it). But even after a priest has accepted it, the priest is not permitted to shut it into a vault [to die], for nowhere is this ever taught regarding a firstborn. And above (Bekhorot 35a) we learned about a male sheep that is old with its wool hanging down, implying that they used to wait until it got a blemish. One may distinguish between a firstborn and one who consecrates nowadays: a firstborn becomes permitted once it gets a blemish, without redemption, so shutting it into a vault would be a loss to consecrated property; but what one consecrates is not permitted even after it gets a blemish without redemption, and if he redeems it he must throw the money away. Therefore when he shuts it into a vault nowadays, there is no loss to consecrated property.

messages.text: This baraita indicates that animals that cannot be sacrificed nowadays must be left to die so that they are not used improperly.
If so, then a firstborn should also not be consecrated, as this too could lead to a mishap.
messages.quote: due to concern that a mishap might occur

notes.he: כיון דמעשר בזמן הזה לא קדיש דחיישינן לתקלה בכור נמי ניחוש לתקלה ולא ליקדש:
notes.en: If so: since tithe is not consecrated nowadays because we are concerned about a mishap, let us be concerned about a mishap with the firstborn too, and let it not be consecrated.

messages.text: Does the matter of the consecration of a firstborn depend on us? The animal is automatically consecrated upon its exit from the womb.

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: Does the firstborn depend on us? Said in astonishment.

messages.text: This is what the questioner is saying: Let us sell the ears of all firstborn animals to gentiles before their births, so that they are not consecrated from the outset. A firstborn animal that is jointly owned by a Jew and a gentile does not become consecrated as a firstborn.

notes.he: הכי פרכינן הואיל וחיישת לתקלה לקנינהו לאודנייהו דאימהות לעובדי כוכבים כי היכי דתיהוי יד עובד כוכבי' באמצע ולא ליתי לידי בכורה:
notes.en: This is what he is saying: this is our challenge: since you are concerned about a mishap, let us transfer ownership of the mothers’ ears to gentiles, so that a gentile has a hand in it, and it will not come to firstborn status.

notes.he: הכי קא אמרינן לקנינהו לאודניהו לעובד כוכבים עד שהן במעי אימן דהוה ליה שותפות עובד כוכבים ולא ליקדש כי היכי דלא ליתי לידי תקלה:
notes.en: This is what we are saying: let us transfer ownership of their ears to a gentile while they are in their mothers’ wombs, so that it becomes a partnership with a gentile and is not consecrated, so that one not come to a mishap.

messages.text: It is possible to act in a different manner, so that the priest does not lose out on his rights to the firstborn animal. One can act in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as he says:

notes.he: בתקנתא אחריתי כדרב יהודה והא עדיפא מהך כדאמרן בפירקא קמא (לעיל בכורות דף ג:) דמש"ה כלאי חיותיה דרב מרי דהוה מקני לאודנייהו לעובד כוכבים משום דמפקע להו אפי' מקדושת כהן:
notes.en: And it answers: it is possible by another remedy, as Rabbi Yehuda says. And this remedy is better than that one, as we said in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 3b): that is why Rav Mari’s animals died out, because he used to transfer ownership of their ears to a gentile, since that removes them even from the priest’s holiness [i.e., the priest loses his gift].

notes.he: לעיל בפ"ק (בכורות דף ג: ד"ה דקא) פירשתי דלדידן שרי לאקנויי לעובד כוכבים כיון דלא ס"ל כרב יהודה:
notes.en: It is possible, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: above in the first chapter (Bekhorot 3b) I explained that for us it is permitted to transfer ownership to a gentile, since we do not hold like Rabbi Yehuda [the print reads “Rav Yehuda”].

messages.text: It is permitted for a person to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn animal fetus before it emerges into the air of the world.

notes.he: לא משום הכי קדיש בכור האידנא דאפשר כדרב יהודה דמטיל בו מום קודם שיצא לאויר העולם ולא יאכל תם:
notes.en: No: the firstborn is consecrated nowadays for this reason, that it is possible to act as Rabbi Yehuda says, inflicting a blemish on it before it emerges into the air of the world, so that it will not be eaten unblemished.

messages.text: If so, here too, it is possible for one to inflict a blemish from the outset, before the animal becomes consecrated as the tithed animal.
messages.quote: inflict a blemish upon a firstborn

notes.he: גבי מעשר אפשר בתקנתא דלא צריך לשהויי דלישדי ביה מומא מעיקרא:
notes.en: Here too: with tithe, a remedy is possible that does not require keeping it: let him inflict a blemish on it from the outset.

notes.he: התם נמי גבי מעשר אפשר דשדי ביה מומא מעיקרא קודם שיצא עשירי והוי בעל מום ולית ביה תקלה וליקדוש:
notes.en: There too, with tithe, it is possible to inflict a blemish on it from the outset, before the tenth comes out, so that it is blemished and there is no mishap with it; so let it be consecrated.

messages.text: How can one know which animal will emerge as the tenth? Since it is impossible to know this, one cannot inflict a blemish on the animal before it becomes consecrated.

notes.he: ומשני מי ידע הי נפיק:
notes.en: And it answers: who knows which will come out?

notes.he: דלישדי ביה מומא מעיקרא וכי תימא כו':
notes.en: Who knows which will come out, so that he could inflict a blemish on it from the outset? And if you say, etc.

messages.text: And if you would say that one should bring out the animal upon which he has inflicted the blemish at the head of the ten animals to ensure that it will be the tithed animal, this is not a valid option, as the Merciful One states: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad.” This means one may not plan in advance which animal will be the tenth.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: בעשירי:
notes.en: At the head of ten: as the tenth.

notes.he: משמע שהוא לא יוציאנו אלא הוא יוצא מעצמו:
notes.en: He shall not inquire: implies that he must not bring it out [himself]; rather, it comes out on its own.

messages.caption: “Whatever passes under the rod”: the animals come out one at a time and whichever happens to be tenth is sacred, so no one can choose it, or blemish it, in advance.

messages.text: And if you would say it is possible to inflict a blemish on the entire herd of animals and thereby ensure the tenth one will be blemished, that is also undesirable. The reason is that soon the Temple will be rebuilt and we will require animals for offerings, and there will be none remaining without a blemish.

notes.dh: וכי תימא אפשר דשדי ביה מומא בכוליה עדריה
notes.he: קודם שיעשר דעדיין הן חולין ומותר להטיל מום ואח"כ יעשר דמעשר חל על בעל מום כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ל״ג) לא יבקר בין טוב לרע:
notes.en: And if you say it is possible to inflict a blemish on his entire herd: before he tithes, while they are still non-sacred and it is permitted to inflict a blemish; and afterward he tithes, for the tithe takes effect on a blemished animal, as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad” (Leviticus 27:33).

messages.text: But here too, with regard to a firstborn animal, why not also say that soon the Temple will be rebuilt and we will require animals for offerings and there will be none remaining without a blemish?

notes.he: דקאמרת יטיל בהן מום איכא למיפרך מהרה יבנה בית המקדש כו':
notes.en: And it challenges: here too, with a firstborn, where you said he may inflict a blemish on them, one can challenge: soon the Temple will be rebuilt, etc.

messages.text: It is possible to bring the offerings from ordinary animals that are not firstborns.
Here too, with regard to the animal tithe, it is possible to bring the offerings from animals purchased from another person, which are exempt from animal tithe, as taught in the mishna on 55b.

notes.he: שהלקוחין א"צ להטיל בהם מום שהרי פטורין מן המעשר דקתני במתני' הלקוח והניתן לו במתנה פטור ממעשר בהמה:
notes.en: Here too it is possible with purchased animals: for purchased animals need no blemish inflicted on them, since they are exempt from the tithe, as the mishna [55b] teaches: an animal purchased or received as a gift is exempt from animal tithe.

messages.text: Since anyone who has animals inflicts a blemish on all of the animals in his herd to avoid consecrating the tithe, there will be very few unblemished animals available for purchase. And furthermore, blemishes that disqualify sacrificial animals are common, as even if the blemish is small, e.g., on the animal’s eyelid, it disqualifies the animal from being used for sacrifice.

notes.dh: ומשני כיון דאיהו שדי מומין בכולי עדריה
notes.he: פטורין הנולדים אצלו הוו לקוחים דבר מועט ושכיחי מומי טובא דפסלי בקדשים ואפי' דוקין שבעין פסלי הלכך לא שכיחי בהמות להקרבה משום הכי לא מפרישינן מעשר:
notes.en: And it answers: since he inflicts blemishes on his whole herd, the exempt ones among his animals, the purchased ones, are few. And blemishes that disqualify for offerings are very common; even the dukin of the eye [Davidson: the eyelid] disqualify. So animals fit to be sacrificed would not be common, and for this reason we do not separate the tithe.

notes.he: בהו מומא בלקוחין ולא שכיחי תמין בלקוחין (כי) לצורך הקרבה הלכך אסיר למישדא מומא בעדריה ומשום הכי לא קדיש מעשר האידנא:
notes.en: And they are common: blemishes are common among purchased animals, and unblemished ones fit for sacrifice are not common among purchased animals. Therefore it is prohibited to inflict blemishes on his herd, and for this reason tithe is not consecrated nowadays.

messages.text: Therefore, it will not be common to find animals fit to be used as offerings. For this reason the Sages decreed that one should not tithe his animals in the present time.

It is obvious that the mitzva to tithe is not in effect with regard to sacrificial animals, as they are not his. Since sacrificial animals have been dedicated to the Temple, of course the owner cannot subsequently consecrate them.
messages.quote: with regard to non-sacred animals but not with regard to sacrificial animals

messages.text: The mishna is referring to offerings of lesser sanctity, e.g., peace offerings, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says: Offerings of lesser sanctity are the monetary property of their owners, and therefore the owner can consecrate them.

The verse: “And he commits a trespass against the Lord,” serves to include one who takes a false oath with regard to offerings of lesser sanctity belonging to another, which are the property of their owners. This is the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
messages.lead: As it is taught in a baraita with regard to the guilt offering of a robber who takes a false oath:

verse.he: נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּיהֹוָה וְכִחֵשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ בְּפִקָּדוֹן אוֹ־בִתְשׂוּמֶת יָד אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת־עֲמִיתוֹ׃
verse.en: When a person sins and commits a trespass against GOD—by dealing deceitfully with another in the matter of a deposit or a pledge, uncertain. or through robbery, or by defrauding another,

notes.he: אצטריך לאשמועינן לרבות קדשים קלים שאם הפקיד אצל חבירו בהמות שלמים וכפרו ונשבע עליה ואח"כ הודה ישלם קרן וחומש ואשם דקרינא ביה בה' ובעמיתו דכתי' ומעלה מעל בה' וכחש בעמיתו ישלם ושלמים יש בהן לה' ובעמיתו:
notes.en: And in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: it was needed to teach us to include offerings of lesser sanctity: if one deposited peace-offering animals with his fellow, and the fellow denied it and swore, and afterward admitted, he pays the principal and a fifth and brings a guilt offering. For we read of it “against the Lord” and “against his fellow,” as it is written: “And he commits a trespass against the Lord and denies to his fellow” (Leviticus 5:21), and peace offerings have a share for the Lord and a share for one’s fellow.

messages.text: Accordingly, it might enter your mind to say that such animals should be tithed. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that the mitzva of animal tithe is not in effect with regard to sacrificial animals at all.
But one can say it is indeed so, i.e., perhaps offerings of lesser sanctity can indeed be tithed.

notes.he: דליעשרו:
notes.en: Here too: let them be tithed.

messages.text: The Merciful One states: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord.” This teaches that this mitzva applies only to an animal that can become sacred in the future but not to an animal that is already sanctified, e.g., that has been set aside as an offering of lesser sanctity.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: עשירי יהיה קדש:
notes.en: Shall be sacred: the tenth shall be sacred.

messages.text: The reason that offerings of lesser sanctity cannot be tithed is that the Merciful One writes: “The tenth shall be sacred to the Lord,” from which it can be inferred that were that not the case, I would say that the sanctity of the animal tithe does take effect on the animal.

notes.he: מפרש לקמן ויעבור עלייהו בלא ימכר ולא יגאל:
notes.en: The sanctity of the tithe: the Gemara explains below: and he would transgress with them “it shall not be sold” and “it shall not be redeemed.”

messages.text: This claim is difficult, as now that consecration of stringent sanctity does not take effect with regard to offerings of lesser sanctity, as will be explained, is it necessary to teach that a consecration of lesser sanctity does not take effect with regard to offerings of lesser sanctity?
What is this halakha that consecration of stringent sanctity does not take effect with regard to offerings of lesser sanctity? As we learned in a mishna:
Both concerning animals consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance, one cannot alter their designation from one form of sanctity to another form of sanctity.

notes.he: שאין קדושת מזבח חלה על קדושת בדה"ב ואע"ג דקדושת מזבח חמורה ולא קדושת בדק הבית על קדושת מזבח שיהא חייב ליתן דמיהן לבדק הבית:
notes.en: From sanctity to sanctity: the sanctity of the altar does not take effect on sanctity for Temple maintenance, even though the altar’s sanctity is more stringent; nor does the sanctity of Temple maintenance take effect on the altar’s sanctity such that he would have to give their value to Temple maintenance.

notes.he: קדושה קלה לחמורה כגון שלמים לעולה:
notes.en: One cannot change it from sanctity to sanctity: from a lesser sanctity to a stringent one, for example from a peace offering to a burnt offering.

messages.text: But one can consecrate an animal already consecrated for the altar by consecration of its value, and that value is donated to the Temple treasury for maintenance, in addition to the sacrificing of the animal. And one can dedicate that value for the purpose of giving it to the priests.

notes.he: קדשי מזבח לקדשי בדק הבית:
notes.en: But one may consecrate: altar offerings for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: טובת הנאה שיש לו מקדושת מזבח יכול ליתן לבדק הבית וזו היא טובת הנאה דיכול ליטול סלע מישראל אחר על מנת שיתננה לבן בתו כהן שיקריבנה כדאמרן בפ' עד כמה (לעיל בכורות דף כז.) עילוי היינו שמעלה בדמים אותו שיעור טובת הנאה ונותן לגזבר:
notes.en: Consecration of value: the benefit [tovat hana’a] he has from the altar’s sanctity he can give to Temple maintenance. That benefit is that he could take a sela from another Israelite on condition that he give the animal to that man’s daughter’s son, a priest, to sacrifice it, as we said in chapter Ad Kamma (above, Bekhorot 27a). Ileui [value] means that he assesses that measure of benefit in money and gives it to the Temple treasurer.

notes.he: בקדשי מזבח מחרימין ויתן לכהן כפי טובת הנאה שיש לו בהן אבל חלק מזבח לא חיילא שום קדושה אחריתי:
notes.en: And they dedicate them: they dedicate altar offerings, and he gives the priest according to the benefit he has in them; but on the altar’s own portion no other sanctity takes effect.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס טובת הנאה שיש לו מקדושת מזבח יכול ליתן לבדק הבית וזו טובת הנאה דיכול ליטול סלע מישראל אחר על מנת שיתננה לבן בתו כהן להקריבה כדאמר בפ' עד כמה (לעיל בכורות דף כז.) עד כאן לשון הקונטרס ובמס' ערכין (דף כח.) מפרש בענין אחר דתנן בהמקדיש שדהו מחרים אדם את קדשיו בין קדשי קדשים בין קדשים קלים אם נדר נותן דמים פירוש שכל דמיו שוין לו דחייב באחריותו ואם נדבה נותן טובתה שור זה עולה אומדים כמה אדם רוצה בשור זה להעלותו עולה שאינו חייב וטובת הנאה דפ' עד כמה (לעיל בכורות דף כז.) לא שייכא אלא בדבר הנאכל כו' דגבי הני קאמר לה התם וכי האי גוונא קתני בערכין (דף כח:) גבי בכור דתנן הבכור בין תם בין בעל מום מחרימין אותו ובאיזה צד פודין אותו אומדים כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בבכור זה ליתנו לבן בתו או לבן אחותו אי נמי גבי דבר שאין נידב ונידר שייכא טובת הנאה זו אבל בדבר הנידר ונידב שייכא אידך טובת הנאה:
notes.en: Consecration of value: the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: the benefit he has from the altar’s sanctity he can give to Temple maintenance, and that benefit is that he could take a sela from another Israelite on condition that he give the animal to that man’s daughter’s son, a priest, to sacrifice it, as stated in chapter Ad Kamma (above, Bekhorot 27a). Thus far the Kuntres. But in tractate Arakhin (28a) it is explained differently, for we learned in HaMakdish Sadehu: a person may dedicate his consecrated items, whether offerings of the most sacred order or of lesser sanctity; if it was a vow, he gives their value, meaning their whole value, since he bears responsibility for them; and if it was a gift offering, he gives its benefit: [if he said] “this ox is a burnt offering,” they assess how much a person would pay for this ox in order to offer it as a burnt offering, which he is not obligated to do. And the benefit of chapter Ad Kamma applies only to something that is eaten, etc., for it is about such things that it is said there. Similarly it teaches in Arakhin (28b) about a firstborn: one may dedicate a firstborn, whether unblemished or blemished; and how does one redeem it? They assess how much a person would give for this firstborn to give it to his daughter’s son or his sister’s son. Alternatively: that kind of benefit applies to something that cannot be vowed or donated, but for something that can be vowed and donated the other kind of benefit applies.

notes.dh: אבל מקדישין הקדש עלוי ומחרימין אותו
notes.he: כיצד כדתנן בערכין בפרק המקדיש מחרים אדם את קדשיו בין קדשי קדשים בין קדשים קלים אם נדר הן דאמר דחייב באחריותן נותן את דמיהן לכהנים מפני שהחרימם. ואם נדבה הן נותן את טובתה לכהנים. כיצד שור זה עולה. היינו נדבה דלא אמר עלי אומדין כמה אדם כהן שאינו ממשמר זה שמשמש רוצה ליתן לבעלים בשור זה שימתין לו עד זמן משמרתו כדי שיעלהו עולה שיזכה בעורו וההוא טובת הנאה יתן לכהנים כשהחרימן. וכן המקדיש את קדשיו הקדש עילוי שמעלה אותן בדמים לבדק הבית אם נדר הם נותן את דמיהן. ואם נדבה נותן את טובתה לגזבר:
notes.en: But one may consecrate them by consecration of value, and dedicate them. How? As we learned in Arakhin, chapter HaMakdish: a person may dedicate his consecrated items, whether offerings of the most sacred order or of lesser sanctity. If they are a vow, that is, he said [“it is upon me”], so that he bears responsibility for them, he gives their value to the priests, since he dedicated them. And if they are a gift offering, he gives its benefit to the priests. How? “This ox is a burnt offering” is a gift offering, since he did not say “upon me.” They assess how much a priest who is not of the serving watch would give the owner for this ox, for him to wait until the priest’s watch, so that he may offer it as a burnt offering and acquire its hide; and that benefit he gives to the priests when he dedicated them. Likewise one who consecrates his consecrated items by consecration of value, assessing them in money for Temple maintenance: if they are a vow, he gives their value; and if a gift offering, he gives its benefit to the treasurer.

messages.text: This mishna teaches that one may not consecrate an animal that has already been consecrated for Temple maintenance as an offering for the altar, despite the fact that an offering has more stringent sanctity, and if so, then the sanctity of the animal tithe certainly does not take effect with regard to offerings of lesser sanctity.

Even so, it is necessary for the mishna to teach that tithes do not take effect on offerings of lesser sanctity, lest you say that there, in the mishna in Temura, the reason is that not every animal stands to potentially become a burnt offering, i.e., an offering of more stringent sanctity, from the time it is born. For this reason the greater sanctity cannot take effect once the animal has been consecrated as an offering of lesser sanctity.
messages.quote: one cannot alter their designation from one form of sanctity to another

notes.he: היינו טעמא דלא חיילא קדושת מזבח אקדושת בדק הבית דכל בהמה לאו לעולה קיימא שהרי רוב בהמות עומדות לאכילה הלכך כי אקדשה לבדק הבית שפיר אקדשה וגמר וחיילא עלה קדושת בדק הבית דתו לא לשנייה לקדשי מזבח אבל לגבי מעשר דכל בהמה למעשר קיימא אע"ג דאקדשה לשלמים לא פקע תורת מעשר מינה:
notes.en: Lest you say: the reason the altar’s sanctity does not take effect on the sanctity of Temple maintenance is that not every animal stands to be a burnt offering, since most animals stand to be eaten. Therefore when he consecrated it for Temple maintenance, he consecrated it properly, and the sanctity of Temple maintenance took full effect on it, so that it can no longer be changed to an altar offering. But with tithe, where every animal stands to be tithe, even though he consecrated it as a peace offering, the law of tithe is not removed from it.

notes.he: הוא דאין משנין דכל בהמה לאו לעולה קיימין דלא חזיא לעולה אלא זכר להכי לא חיילא אשאר קדשים:
notes.en: Lest you say there: that is why one cannot change it, since not every animal stands to be a burnt offering, as only a male is fit for a burnt offering; therefore it does not take effect on other offerings.

messages.text: But in the mishna here, where every animal stands to potentially become an animal tithe offering, one might have thought that even though it is consecrated as an offering of lesser sanctity, nevertheless the initial potential prohibition, i.e., status, of animal tithe is not abrogated from it.

notes.he: גבי מעשר דכל בהמה למעשר קיימין בין זכר בין נקבה:
notes.en: But here: with tithe, every animal stands to be tithe, whether male or female.

messages.text: What difference is there if an animal that has been consecrated as a peace offering is also sanctified as an animal tithe offering?

notes.he: אי הוה חיילא קדושת מעשר אשלמים הא לא חמיר מעשר משלמים:
notes.en: And what difference does it make, if the sanctity of tithe took effect on a peace offering? For tithe is not more stringent than a peace offering.

notes.he: אי קדושת מעשר חיילא אמוקדשין על שלמים דמאי קדושה חמורה איכא במעשר דליתיה בקדשים קלים:
notes.en: What difference does it make, if the sanctity of tithe takes effect on consecrated animals, on peace offerings? For what stringent sanctity is there in tithe that is not in offerings of lesser sanctity?

messages.text: If it is sanctified as an animal tithe offering, the prohibition of: “It shall not be redeemed,” and the prohibition of: It shall not be sold (see 32b), take effect. A peace offering can be redeemed, whereas it is prohibited to redeem or sell animal tithe even after its slaughter. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that the sanctity of animal tithe does not take effect on animals that have been consecrated as offerings of lesser sanctity.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.dh: למיקם עלה בלא ימכר ולא יגאל
notes.he: דשלמים הוו בני פדיון קמשמע לן יהיה קדש ולא שכבר קדש:
notes.en: To make it subject to “it shall not be sold” and “it shall not be redeemed”: for peace offerings can be redeemed [when blemished]. It teaches us: “shall be sacred,” and not what is already sacred.

notes.dh: איכא למיקם עליה בלא יגאל ולא ימכר
notes.he: קדשים קלים אית להו פדיון ומעשר בהמה לית ליה:
notes.en: To make it subject to “it shall not be redeemed” and “it shall not be sold”: offerings of lesser sanctity can be redeemed, and animal tithe cannot.

messages.text: In this regard the Gemara cites a baraita:
messages.quote: And it is in effect with regard to the herd and the flock, but they are not tithed from one for the other; and with regard to sheep and goats, and they are tithed from one for the other

messages.text: Let it be proven that the animals from the new flock and the animals from the old flock can be tithed from one for the other, by an a fortiori inference: And if sheep and goats, which are prohibited for interbreeding with each other due to the prohibition of diverse kinds, are nevertheless tithed from one for the other, with regard to animals from the new flock and the old flock, which are not prohibited for interbreeding with each other as diverse kinds, is it not logical that they should be tithed from one for the other?

Therefore, the verse states: “You shall tithe a tithe from all the increase of your seed that the field brings forth year by year. And you shall eat before the Lord your God, in the place that He shall choose to place His name there, the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herds and of your flocks; that you may learn to fear the Lord your God always.”

verse.he: עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר אֵת כׇּל־תְּבוּאַת זַרְעֶךָ הַיֹּצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה שָׁנָה שָׁנָה׃ וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ׀ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כׇּל־הַיָּמִים׃
verse.en: You shall set aside every year a tenth part of all the yield of your sowing that is brought from the field. You shall consume the tithes of your new grain and wine and oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the ETERNAL your God, in the place where [God] will choose to establish the divine name, so that you may learn to revere the ETERNAL your God forever.

notes.he: הכא אתיא היקישא ומפקא מק"ו ולעיל (גבי) כל פסולי המוקדשין (דף לג.) אתי ק"ו ומפיק מהיקישא גבי פלוגתא דבית שמאי ובית הלל דשרו בית הלל אפי' לזרים ושם (ד"ה וב"ה) פירשתי:
notes.en: The verse states: You shall tithe a tithe: here a juxtaposition comes and overrides the a fortiori inference, while above, in Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 33a), the a fortiori inference comes and overrides the juxtaposition, in the dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, where Beit Hillel permit [the disqualified firstborn] even to non-priests; and there I explained it.

messages.text: Here, the verse is speaking of two tithes; one is the animal tithe and the other one is the grain tithe. And the verse juxtaposes the animal tithe to the grain tithe, teaching that just as the grain tithe is not taken from the new grain for the old grain, so too, the animal tithe is not taken from the new flock for the old flock.

notes.dh: מה מעשר דגן מחדש על הישן לא
notes.he: דכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ב) היוצא השדה שנה שנה היוצא שנה אתה מעשר ולא משנה זו לשנה שעברה ולא משנה שעברה לשנה הבאה:
notes.en: Just as grain tithe is not taken from the new for the old: as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:22): “that the field brings forth year by year.” From what comes out in a year you tithe, and not from this year for the past year, nor from the past year for the coming year.

notes.dh: מה מעשר דגן מחדש אישן לא
notes.he: כדאמרינן בספרי והרמותם ממנו מן המובחר ולא ממין על שאינו מינו ולא מחדש אישן ותרומה איתקש למעשר דכתיב כן תרימו גם אתם מכל מעשרותיכם:
notes.en: Just as grain tithe is not taken from new for old: as we say in the Sifrei: “and you shall set apart from it”: from the best, and not from one type for another, and not from new for old. And teruma is juxtaposed to tithe, as it is written: “So you also shall set apart … from all your tithes” (Numbers 18:28).

messages.text: If so, let us say with regard to sheep and goats that they too are not tithed for each other, by the same reasoning, i.e., that the verse juxtaposes the animal tithe to the grain tithe: Just as grain tithe is not separated from one type of grain for another grain that is not its type, so too, animal tithe is not separated from one type of animal for another species of animal that is not its type.
messages.quote: juxtaposes the animal tithe to the grain tithe

notes.dh: מה מעשר דגן ממין על שאינו מינו לא
notes.he: כדאמרינן לקמן תן חלב לזה ולזה:
notes.en: Just as grain tithe is not taken from one type for another: as we say below: give the best of this and the best of that.

messages.text: With regard to animal tithe the Merciful One has amplified the halakha by stating “flock.” This teaches that all species referred to with the term flock, i.e., sheep and goats, are tithed together.

notes.he: דמשמע כל צאן מין אחד חשוב לענין מעשר:
notes.en: And flock: implies that all flock counts as one species with regard to tithe.

messages.text: If so, let us also say that new flocks are tithed together with old flocks, based on that amplification of the verse.

notes.he: לירבי מוצאן:
notes.en: If so, new and old too: let them be included from “flock.”

messages.text: It is written: “You shall tithe a tithe,” to teach that old and new flocks are not tithed together.

verse.he: עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר אֵת כׇּל־תְּבוּאַת זַרְעֶךָ הַיֹּצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה שָׁנָה שָׁנָה׃
verse.en: You shall set aside every year a tenth part of all the yield of your sowing that is brought from the field.

notes.he: דאתקש למעשר דגן:
notes.en: But it is written: You shall tithe a tithe: which is juxtaposed to the grain tithe.

messages.text: And what did you see that led you to use the juxtaposition to prohibit tithing old and new flocks together but not to prohibit tithing sheep and goats together?

The verse states: “Year by year,” which teaches that I have juxtaposed the flocks with regard to the year in which they were born, i.e., to prohibit tithing old and new flocks together, but not with regard to another matter.

notes.he: מעשר בהמה למעשר דגן שלא יתרום משל שנה שעברה שנולד קודם אלול על שנולדו לאחר אלול:
notes.en: I juxtaposed it with regard to the year: animal tithe to grain tithe, that he not separate from last year’s, born before Elul, for those born after Elul.

notes.he: מין במינו:
notes.en: And not for another matter: [such as] one type with its own type.

notes.he: מעשר בהמה למעשר דגן מה מעשר דגן אין מעשרין משנה זו על זו אף מעשר בהמה נמי:
notes.en: I juxtaposed it with regard to the year: animal tithe to grain tithe. Just as grain tithe is not tithed from one year for another, so too animal tithe.

notes.he: כלומר דמין על שאינו מינו מעשרין:
notes.en: And not for another matter: that is, one may tithe from one type for another that is not its type.

messages.caption: What may be tithed together, and the verse behind each answer.

messages.text: One may not separate the portion of the produce designated for the priest [teruma] from one type of produce to exempt another type of produce that is not its type, and if one did separate teruma in that manner, his teruma is not teruma.

notes.he: במעשר דגן קמיירי:
notes.en: One may not separate teruma: this speaks of the tithes of produce.

messages.text: From where is this matter derived?

messages.alt: and some say: Rabbi Ami says that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says
messages.text: The verse states with regard to teruma: “All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the grain, the first part of them, which they give to the Lord, to you have I given them.” The Torah says: Give the best, i.e., teruma and tithes, of this, the oil, and the best of that, the wine, separately, i.e., one may not give teruma or tithes from one for the other. This mitzva also applies to tithes, as it too is called: “The best” (Numbers 18:30).

verse.he: כֹּל חֵלֶב יִצְהָר וְכׇל־חֵלֶב תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן רֵאשִׁיתָם אֲשֶׁר־יִתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה לְךָ נְתַתִּים׃
verse.en: All the best of the new oil, wine, and grain—the choice parts that they present to GOD—I give to you.

notes.he: היינו תרומה ומעשר כדכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ל׳) בהרימכם את חלבו ממנו וקאמר רחמנא שיתן לכל אחד מעשרותיו בפני עצמו:
notes.en: Give the best of this and the best of that: that is, teruma and tithe, as it is written (Numbers 18:30): “when you set apart its best from it”; and the Merciful One says that he must give each one its own tithes separately.

messages.text: Continues on 54a: the Gemara asks where it learns that wine and grain, or one grain and another, may not be tithed for each other, and proposes an a fortiori inference.
